steps: Lie on your back with the head supported and shoulders relaxed.
Rest the base of the skull on a towel roll and breathe with the jaw relaxed.
Move only until you feel a gentle stretch, not a pinch.
Hold for several slow breaths, then return to center.
Repeat on the other side if the stretch is one-sided.
tips: Keep the jaw and shoulders relaxed so the neck does not tense up.
Keep the stretch gentle and slow.
Do not bounce or force the end range.
Breathe steadily and aim for a mild pull rather than pain.
Keep the towel loose enough to guide the stretch or tension without forcing the joint.
Warm up first or do these after activity if holding a longer static stretch.

Reach one foot back onto the step and press through it carefully.
Press through the stepping foot to stand tall on the step.
Step back down with control and repeat, switching sides as planned.
tips: Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes.
Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches.
Choose a range where you can keep control and balance.
Move under control, breathe steadily, and stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, or joint pinching.

items.description: Stand on a step and slowly lower one heel toward the floor before rising.
items.name: Step-Down
steps: Stand on a low step or stair with one foot near the edge.
Shift weight into the standing leg and slowly lower the other heel toward the floor.
Tap lightly if comfortable while keeping the standing knee aligned over the toes.
Press through the standing foot to return to the top.
tips: Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes.
Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches.
Choose a range where you can keep control and balance.
Move under control, breathe steadily, and stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, or joint pinching.

items.description: Take three to five seconds lowering from a step, keeping knee aligned.
items.name: Slow Eccentric Step-Down
steps: Stand on a low step or stair with one foot near the edge.
Shift weight into the standing leg and slowly lower the other heel toward the floor.
Tap lightly if comfortable while keeping the standing knee aligned over the toes.
Press through the standing foot to return to the top.
Take extra time on the lowering phase and avoid dropping quickly.
tips: Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes.
Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches.
Choose a range where you can keep control and balance.
Move under control, breathe steadily, and stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, or joint pinching.

items.description: Step diagonally back like a skater and tap the rear foot lightly.
items.name: Skater Step-Back
steps: Stand tall with feet about hip-width apart and a little space around you.
Brace lightly and begin the movement slowly so you understand the range.
Step diagonally back like a skater and tap the rear foot lightly.
Return to the start position and repeat for the planned reps, time, or side.
tips: Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes.
Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches.
Choose a range where you can keep control and balance.
Move under control, breathe steadily, and stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, or joint pinching.

items.description: Jump from a split stance and land back in the same lunge position.
items.name: Split Lunge Jump
steps: Stand tall with feet under hips and brace your trunk.
Step into the lunge with one foot and lower until both knees bend comfortably.
Keep the front knee tracking over the middle toes and your torso controlled.
Push through the front foot to return to standing.
Add a small hop only after you stand tall, then land softly and reset.
tips: Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes.
Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches.
Choose a range where you can keep control and balance.
Land with soft knees and stop plyometric reps before landings get loud or stiff.
Move under control, breathe steadily, and stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, or joint pinching.

Brace your trunk and keep your spine long.
Pull elbows back toward your ribs while squeezing shoulder blades.
Lower the load or release tension with control.
tips: Start each pull by setting shoulder blades gently back and down.
Avoid shrugging or craning your neck.
Move slowly enough to feel the upper back, not momentum.
Keep the load secure and close enough that it does not pull you out of position.
Move under control, breathe steadily, and stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, or joint pinching.

items.description: Lie on back, brace gently, and lower opposite arm and leg without arching.

steps: Lie on your back with arms reaching toward the ceiling and knees stacked over hips at about 90 degrees.

Return to the start position and repeat on the other side.

Move under control, breathe steadily, and stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, or joint pinching.

steps: Lie on your back with your ribs relaxed down and your lower back comfortable. Set up your broomstick before you start and make sure it will not slide or tip.
Move slowly into the stretch or mobility position until you feel mild tension, not pain.
Hold a stick and move arms overhead while ribs stay heavy.
Breathe steadily, then ease out and switch sides if the movement is one-sided.
tips: Look for stretch or motion, not pinching in the shoulder joint.
Keep ribs from flaring to fake extra range.
Use a wider grip or smaller range when shoulders feel tight.
A good stretch feels like mild to moderate tension, not sharp pain.

Use a wider grip or smaller range when shoulders feel tight.
A good stretch feels like mild to moderate tension, not sharp pain.

Move slowly into the stretch or mobility position until you feel mild tension, not pain.

Back off if you feel numbness, tingling, or sharp wrist pain.
Move each finger, wrist, or elbow slowly through a comfortable range.
A good stretch feels like mild to moderate tension, not sharp pain.

items.description: From all fours, alternate rounding and arching the spine with slow breathing.

Move back and forth slowly with your breath.

Move through the upper back and ribs without forcing the low back.
Keep the range comfortable and avoid aggressive end-range pushing.

steps: Start in a comfortable lunge stance with one foot forward, one leg back, and hands on the floor or hips as needed.
Bend one knee and hold the foot, ankle, or place the shin against the wall/couch as listed.
Tuck your pelvis slightly and keep knees reasonably close.
Hold the front-of-thigh stretch, then release and switch sides.
tips: Keep knee and toes pointing in the same general direction.
Use a soft bend in the knee when a straight-leg stretch feels too intense.
Ease in gradually; do not bounce into hamstring, calf, or groin stretches.
A good stretch feels like mild to moderate tension, not sharp pain.

items.description: From pigeon, bend the back knee and gently hold the foot if comfortable.
items.name: Pigeon Quad Stretch
steps: Set up in a comfortable pigeon position with one shin forward and the other leg behind you.
Bend the back knee and reach for the back foot only if comfortable.
Gently draw the heel toward your glute while keeping the front hip supported.
Release slowly and switch sides.
tips: Keep knee and toes pointing in the same general direction.
Use a soft bend in the knee when a straight-leg stretch feels too intense.
Ease in gradually; do not bounce into hamstring, calf, or groin stretches.
A good stretch feels like mild to moderate tension, not sharp pain.

items.description: Sit tall, loop towel around foot, and pull toes back with knee straight.

Keep the knee straight or bent depending on the variation.

tips: Keep knee and toes pointing in the same general direction.

Ease in gradually; do not bounce into hamstring, calf, or groin stretches.

items.description: Lie with both legs up the wall and open them into a gentle V.

Keep the opposite leg bent or long in a comfortable position.
Straighten the raised knee only as far as you can without strain.
Breathe, then lower and switch sides.

Use a soft bend in the knee when a straight-leg stretch feels too intense.
Ease in gradually; do not bounce into hamstring, calf, or groin stretches.
Make sure the support surface is stable and positioned so you can exit easily.
